Information since the previous meeting suggests ongoing labor-market strength and solid real activity despite transitory hurricane-related supply disruptions—an assessment consistent with New Keynesian policy frameworks in which rate setters “look through” temporary cost-push shocks while smoothing interest-rate adjustments (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler; Taylor rule). The emphasis on soft core inflation and low market-based inflation compensation fits evidence of price stickiness and anchored expectations under credible policy (Nakamura and Steinsson; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), while the Committee’s symmetric 2 percent objective and close monitoring of inflation align with inflation-targeting best practices. Holding the federal funds rate at 1–1¼ percent, paired with guidance for gradual increases, reflects standard interest-rate smoothing and forward-guidance implementation (Goodfriend, 2002), and the continuation of balance-sheet normalization is consistent with literature that QE and its unwind primarily operate through term-premium channels rather than large effects on real growth (Cochrane and Piazzesi; QE evidence). Overall, the tone is moderately positive on growth and employment but cautious on inflation, warranting a slightly positive sentiment.
